title: Expanding the trilayer Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate family: Synthesis and characterization of Sm$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10-δ}$ single crystals
authors: Yuhang Zhang, Tian-Yi Li, Xiyu Zhu, Ying-Jie Zhang, Shengtai Fan, Qing Li, Hai-Hu Wen
abstract: The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelates has attracted significant attention. Bulk superconductivity emerges under pressure in trilayer nickelates La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10-δ}$ (T$_c$ $\approx$ 30 K) and Pr$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10-δ}$ (T$_c$ $\approx$ 40.5 K), where the reduced ionic radius of Pr$^{3+}$ may generate internal chemical pressure and enhance T$_c$. However, synthesizing trilayer RP phases with smaller rare-earth elements (Ln) is extremely challenging. So far, only the La, Pr, and Nd analogues have been synthesized with stable phases in the single rare-earth form. Here we report the first successful high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) synthesis of samarium-based compound Sm$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10-δ}$. Magnetization and transport measurements consistently confirm a density wave (DW) transition at ~180 K at ambient pressure. Through a careful fitting to the structural data of Sm$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10-δ}$, it is found that the bond angle of (Ni-O-Ni) associating with the interlayer apical oxygen is much smaller than 180$^{\circ}$, which was assumed to be the key factor for the occurrence of superconductivity. By applying pressures up to 80 GPa, despite partial suppression of insulating behavior and the DW order, but superconductivity is not observed in our present study. Density functional theory calculations suggest that the 3d$_{z^2}$ and 3d$_{x^2-y^2}$ are separated from other t$_{2g}$ orbitals and make a primary contribution to the Fermi surface. The newly synthesized trilayer nickelate Sm$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10-δ}$ offers a unique platform for probing the fundamental physics of RP nickelates.
summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of the trilayer nickelate $	ext{Sm}_4	ext{Ni}_3	ext{O}_{10-\delta}$, expanding the study of this superconducting material class. While the material shows a density wave transition, superconductivity is not observed even under extreme pressure. The authors argue that significant structural distortions, particularly in the $	ext{Ni-O-Ni}$ bond angle, are the primary physical mechanism suppressing superconductivity in this system.
main_problem: The study aims to expand the understanding of high-temperature superconductivity in the trilayer Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelate family, specifically by synthesizing and characterizing the Sm$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{10-\delta}$ compound.
main_result: The synthesized $	ext{Sm}_4	ext{Ni}_3	ext{O}_{10-\delta}$ exhibits a density wave (DW) transition at ambient pressure, but superconductivity was not observed even under high pressure (up to 80 GPa), suggesting structural distortions are key barriers.
method: The research combines experimental techniques, including High-Pressure/High-Temperature (HPHT) synthesis, transport/magnetization measurements, and structural characterization (XRD), with theoretical calculations using Density Functional Theory (DFT).
model_or_system: The physical system is the trilayer Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate $	ext{Sm}_4	ext{Ni}_3	ext{O}_{10-\delta}$. The electronic behavior is governed by the correlated Ni $3d$ orbitals, and the structural analysis focuses on the $	ext{Ni-O-Ni}$ bond angle and octahedral distortions.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), Density Wave (DW) transition temperature ($\sim 180 	ext{ K}$), $	ext{Ni-O-Ni}$ bond angle, and electrical/magnetic transport anomalies under pressure.
important_parameters: High pressure (up to 80 GPa), rare-earth element size (Sm vs La/Pr), and the degree of octahedral distortion.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the deviation of the $	ext{Ni-O-Ni}$ bond angle from $180^\circ$ is the key structural factor inhibiting superconductivity in this series.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate structural analysis (crystal structure, bond angle variation), electrical transport (resistance anomalies at 180 K), and magnetization measurements showing magnetic transitions corresponding to the electronic changes.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of literature review (contextualizing RP nickelates), synthesis and structural characterization of $	ext{Sm}_4	ext{Ni}_3	ext{O}_{10-\delta}$, detailed measurements (transport, magnetism, high pressure), and theoretical interpretation linking structural distortions to electronic properties.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physics of strongly correlated electron systems, particularly high-Tc superconductivity, by linking subtle structural changes (bond angles, distortions) to emergent electronic states (DW, superconductivity), which is a major theme in condensed matter theory.
